request: a broom racing game at a magic school where I dodge storm clouds and grab sparks

design.pitch: Race a broom through a wizard-school night sky for 50 seconds, dodging storm clouds and flapping spellbooks and skimming past them for Whoosh points.
design.verb: Tap the left or right side to swerve one lane at a time across five lanes, slipping between falling hazards and under falling sparks.
design.twist: Nerve pays: a hazard that passes in the next lane over (within 80 px) is a near miss worth 'Whoosh +5', so the best line runs right beside danger while sparks build a Streak.
arc: 0–10 s: the first storm cloud drops at 0.7 s, then one cloud about every second at 230 px/s, with mint sparks falling in the five lanes every 900 ms.

10–40 s: the ease_in_out curve kicks in: from about 16 s runaway spellbooks sway across their lane, from about 20 s a second cloud often fills another lane in the same row, and speed and spawn rate climb.
40 s+: difficulty peaks at 45 s (420 px/s, a row every 540 ms); the finish lanterns appear at 47 s and sweep down to the line at 50 s.
design.lose: Three hits from storm clouds or spellbooks; each hit costs one of 3 lives, resets the Streak, clears hazards within 56 px and gives 1 s of grace.
design.win: Survive until the 50-second finish. Score counts sparks (10 + 5 x Streak, Streak up to 8) plus 5 for every Whoosh near miss.
juice: Grabbing a spark: a triangle-wave chime that climbs a whole step with each Streak, and a '+N' pop above the rider.
A near miss: a sine swish sliding from E6 to A5, 10 lavender particles between broom and hazard, a light haptic and 'Whoosh +5'.
The finish: the progress rail fills, the lantern arch sweeps down over the last 3 seconds, then the 'tada' win sting.
design.look: A wizard-academy night race over an indigo sky with a crescent moon and castle spires with warm windows; drifting wisps and speed streaks that stretch as it speeds up. Deep night palette with amber and mint glows: the plum-cloaked rider with an orange scarf reads warm amber, the slate storm clouds with pink lightning and crimson flapping spellbooks read as danger, sparks are mint. Font: Optima.
design.voice: Whimsical and breathless, short race calls: 'Whoosh +5', 'Dodge storm clouds and runaway spellbooks, grab sparks to build a streak, and skim past hazards for Whoosh points.', 'Cross the finish lanterns in 50 seconds.'

brief.intent: Swerve a broom between five lanes through a speeding night race, dodging storm clouds and runaway spellbooks while chaining sparks

why_its_good: Fun at once and harder each second: the first hazard falls at 0.7 s, and `difficulty_curve` (ease_in_out over 45 s) drives fall speed from 230 to 420 px/s, halves the spawn gap, brings in spellbooks that sway toward the next lane at 25% and double rows at 40%, before the finish lanterns at 50 s.

The score rewards nerve: sparks pay 10 + 5 x Streak with a pitch that climbs a whole step per streak (`note: "= 587.0 * pow(1.0595, min(combo, 12) * 2.0)"`), and skimming a hazard in the next lane pays a 'Whoosh +5' near-miss bonus with its own swish, particles and haptic.

A full original art set with depth: a layered night backdrop (crescent moon, aurora haze, castle spires with lit windows), drifting wisps and speed streaks that scroll with `travel`, 2-frame spellbook and spark sprites, a course-progress rail, a finish arch that sweeps down in the last 3 s, floating score pops and its own minor-key music loop.
pitfalls_avoided: Wires `combo` with `bind` (`hit_good -> point`, `hit_bad -> hit`) instead of new events; the streak bonus rule reads `combo` after the fragment's own rule has already raised it.
Keeps hazards in the game's own list and hands them to `collide` through `colliders()`; the game's `hit` rule removes the hazard near `hit_at`, so one cloud costs one life.
The rising-pitch sound is the game's own feedback on `point`, which replaces score's library pickup moment instead of playing both.
Stays within 3 hud_top nodes (lives, score, combo); course progress is a playfield rail, not a fourth HUD node (`A_SLOT_FULL`).

request: a space fighter flying down a narrow canyon shooting drones, with a big boss target at the end

design.pitch: Fly a starfighter down a canyon that keeps narrowing, shred three waves of drones and then blow up the Rift Core, all with one finger.
design.verb: Drag left and right to glide the auto-firing starfighter under drones, dodging their orbs and keeping off the canyon walls.
design.twist: The canyon walls are hazards that close in each wave (the same `wall_l`/`wall_r` draw them and test hits), and wave 4 is a boss: the Rift Core with 24 HP and 3-orb volleys.
arc: 0–10 s: 'Drones inbound' for 1.8 s, then wave 1: 9 weaving scouts launched every 420 ms down a wide canyon while the ship fires twin bolts every 200 ms.
10–40 s: 'Wave 2 incoming' adds homing divers (12 drones), 'Wave 3 incoming' adds gunners that fire aimed orbs (15 drones); the scroll speeds from 200 to 260 px/s and the canyon narrows each wave.
40 s+: 'Rift Core ahead!': the core drifts down, sways across the narrowest canyon yet and fires 3-orb volleys every 1.3 s while 6 more drones come in, until its HP bar is empty.
design.lose: Three hits from drones, orbs or scraping the canyon wall; each costs one of 3 lives, clears drones and orbs within 48 px, resets the chain and gives 1.2 s of grace.
design.win: Clear all 4 waves by breaking the Rift Core. Score: 10 + 5 x chain per drone (chain up to x10, reset by a hit or an escaped drone), 5 per bolt on the core and 300 + 100 x lives left when it breaks.
juice: Each drone down: a square-wave blip that rises with the chain, 16 pink and 6 yellow particles, a '+N' pop, a light haptic and 'Chain xN' bouncing in the bottom HUD.
Hitting the core: yellow sparks and a short tick that drops in pitch as its 24 HP drain, with the RIFT CORE bar shrinking.
Core down: 88 particles, a 12 px shake, a heavy haptic, a sawtooth slide from C4 to C2 and 'CORE DOWN +N' in big text.
design.look: A sunset canyon run: plum rock walls with glowing orange rims and an inner shade layer over a deep rift with an ember river. Dusky plum palette with hot ember and yellow accents: the white-and-cyan starfighter is the only cool color, against magenta drones with amber eyes, orange orbs and a hexagonal yellow Rift Core. Font: Futura.
design.voice: Terse, heroic flight-briefing calls: 'Drones inbound', 'Wave 3 incoming', 'Rift Core ahead!'

brief.intent: Fly a starfighter down a narrowing canyon, shoot four waves of drones and break the Rift Core

why_its_good: A real campaign in about 30 s: `waves` (end_on 'clear', 4 waves) adds a drone type per wave (weaving scouts, homing divers, gunners firing aimed orbs), speeds the scroll and narrows the canyon. Wave 4 is the Rift Core with an HP bar and 3-orb volleys, and breaking it emits `enemies_gone` to win. Break banners ('Wave 3 incoming', 'Rift Core ahead!') pace the run.

One finger, plenty of skill: the ship auto-fires and you drag it sideways (glide mode, so it banks). A chain multiplier (+5 per kill up to x10, reset by a hit or an escaped drone) and a lives bonus on the core reward clean, aggressive play; bots scored from 225 to 2,920.

The canyon is drawn and checked by the same pure functions (`wall_l(y)`, `wall_r(y)`): scrolling `poly` walls with a lit rim and inner shade layer, so what you see is what hits you. Drone variants are frames of one sprite picked with `frame`, and the core is a 2-frame pulsing sprite with a scale pop on each hit.
pitfalls_avoided: Wall contact reuses `collide`: `colliders()` returns `[player]` while the ship is inside a wall, so walls get the same grace, particles, shake and life loss as drones, with no hand-rolled `hit`.
Bolt hits are computed with `let` before any `remove`, so the bolts and drones removed come from the same snapshot; each kill emits `drone_down {x, y}` and particles read `event.x`.
Score is the game's own `score` state plus `objectives.score`, shown as one number in hud_top, because lives + 'Score: N' + 'Wave n of 4' would be wider than the canvas.
Random rolls (`chance`, `random_float`) live only in rule effects; `canyon_cx`, `colliders` and every presentation expression stay pure.

request: an endless runner where I jump across city rooftops at night collecting letters

design.pitch: Sprint across night rooftops as a courier, hopping vents and leaping alleys to grab glowing letters, and see how far you get before three stumbles.
design.verb: Tap to jump and tap again in the air to double-jump, timing hops over vents and stacks and leaps across alleys.
design.twist: Letters float in arcs that trace the ideal jump over each alley, so collecting them teaches the line, and a double jump rescues a late tap.
arc: 0–10 s: three letters wait on the first roof; low vents and alleys 58–86 px wide come at 250 px/s, and a single hop clears either.
10–40 s: the city speeds up on an ease_in curve; the first 100 m milestone pays +50 about 16 s in, and from about 29 s tall stacks need a higher jump or a double-jump.
40 s+: alleys widen by up to 54 px and the run climbs toward 490 px/s at 75 s, a +50 every 100 m, until three stumbles end it.
design.lose: Three stumbles: running into a vent or stack, or landing in an alley (which bounces you back up with 'Whoa!'), each costs one of 3 lives and resets the combo.
design.win: Endless: the score counts letters (10 + 5 x combo, combo up to 6) plus 50 for every 100 m run.
juice: A letter grab: a square-wave note that climbs a whole step per combo, 12 cyan particles and a '+N' pop by the courier.
Every 100 m: the level sting, 24 gold particles, '100 m  +50' in big text and the meter counter bouncing.
Falling into an alley: a red 'Whoa!', a triangle slide from G4 up to C6 and the courier flung back up onto the roof.
design.look: Night rooftops under a violet-to-magenta dusk: a far skyline with warm windows, haze bands drifting at 0.12x, purple brick facades and alleys scrolling at full speed. Moody neon-noir palette: the courier in a yellow jacket and teal cap is warm gold, the steel roof vents with red warning lights and hazard stripes read red, and the letters glow cyan. Font: Avenir Next.
design.voice: Upbeat and street-quick, a few words at a time: 'Whoa!', '100 m  +50', 'The city speeds up the farther you go. Three stumbles ends the run.'

brief.intent: Time jumps across night rooftops, hopping vents and leaping alleys, while collecting glowing letters in arcs

why_its_good: Jump timing with depth: vents need a hop, AC stacks a higher one, alleys need you to land past the far edge, and the double jump rescues a late tap. Letters float in arcs that trace the ideal jump over each alley, which teaches the line by rewarding it.

Endless with a real fail and a real curve: `difficulty_curve` (ease_in over 75 s) takes the run from 250 to 490 px/s and widens the alleys, and three stumbles end it. In the bot gate, runs lasted 7 to 124 s and the best score was 30 times the worst.

Layered city with motion: a static far skyline in the backdrop, haze bands that drift at 0.12x, brick facades and alleys that scroll at full speed, a 2-frame running courier, `ground` role ledge, a +50 milestone every 100 m with a level sting, and a meter counter in hud_bottom.
pitfalls_avoided: Alleys go through `collide` too: `colliders()` adds the player's point while it stands over a gap, and the game's `hit` rule (`when: over_gap()`) bounces the runner out through the public `vel_y` and `player`, so a fall costs a life but never strands the run.
Two obstacle heights become one or two collider points with `fold(blocks, [], (acc, b) => concat(acc, ...))`, instead of a second collide fragment.
No `time_limit` on an endless game; `lives` is the lose path, and `playtest.progress` (score + lives + meters) tells the bots what doing better means.
Labels kept short ('Combo', max 6) so lives + score + combo fit the hud_top row at 4-digit scores.

request: a cozy one-more-try game where you stack cake layers as high as you can

design.pitch: Tap to drop each sliding cake layer, line it up or lose the overhang, and build 24 layers high to put the cherry on top.
design.verb: Tap to drop the layer sliding back and forth above the cake, timing it to line up with the layer below.
design.twist: Whatever hangs over the edge is sliced off and tumbles away, so every sloppy drop makes the cake narrower, but a perfect drop (within 7 px) grows it back by 8 px.
arc: 0–10 s: the first layers on the lilac cake stand; the slider moves at 110 px/s plus 6 per layer, and its outline turns white when it lines up, so early perfects are easy.
10–40 s: past layer 10 the camera glides up, the slider passes 170 px/s, sloppy drops trim the cake thinner and perfect drops grow it back and build the Combo.
40 s+: the climb to the Cherry line at 24 layers on a narrow cake, with the slider at up to 254 px/s; a full miss is a 'Splat!'.
design.lose: Three layers that miss the cake entirely ('Splat!') use up the 3 lives and the bakery closes.
design.win: Stack 24 layers and the cherry pops on top, adding 100 x lives left. Score: 10 per layer that lands, plus 10 x Combo for perfect drops (Combo up to 8).
juice: Every landing: a triangle note that rises with the cake's height, a puff of 10 crumbs and a light haptic.
A perfect drop: a sine chime that climbs with the combo, white and gold particles from both edges, the layer bouncing to 1.08x, a 'Perfect! +N' pop and a sparkle that keeps spinning on that layer.
The cherry: the level sting, the cherry scaling in from 0.2 to 1.3 to 1, and 30 pink particles.
design.look: A cozy morning bakery: peach wallpaper with little diamonds, bunting, jars on shelves and a wooden counter. Warm pastel palette: sponge layers in strawberry, matcha, lemon, cocoa and blueberry with cream frosting drips and a jam line; the sliding layer gets a white outline when aligned, guide lines mark the top layer's edges, and sliced pieces tumble away spinning. Font: Chalkboard SE.
design.voice: Sweet and gently teasing, like a bakery chalkboard: 'Splat!', 'Cherry line', 'Stack 24 layers to add the cherry; three layers on the floor and the bakery closes.'

brief.intent: Drop sliding cake layers onto a growing cake; overhang gets sliced off, perfect drops grow it back, reach 24 layers for the cherry

why_its_good: One tap, understood at a glance: the overhang slices off and tumbles away, so every sloppy drop makes the next one harder. Perfect drops (within 7 px) grow the layer back by 8 px, chain a combo worth 10 more per step and ring a chime that climbs with the combo.

A gentle curve for a calm game: the slider speeds up 6 px/s per layer (110 to 260), the camera glides up as the cake grows, and a ruler with a 'Cherry line' shows the goal. Three dropped layers end it; at 24 layers a cherry pops on top and lives left pay a bonus.

Feedback a player can read: the sliding layer's outline turns white when it lines up, guide lines mark the top layer's edges, perfect layers keep a spinning sparkle, crumbs burst on every landing, and five pastel flavors cycle through list tokens (`$sponge[l.flavor]`).
pitfalls_avoided: Layers are drawn from engine shapes (`rect`, `circle`) so they can be any width; a stretched sprite would squash the frosting drips.
The win waits for a `topper` event 900 ms after the 24th layer, so the last point and combo bonus land before the objective is checked.
The perfect chime is one `note` with a Hz expression; jingle `notes` must be literal note names, or validation fails with E_PRESENTATION.
The drop input has a guard (`when: not built`) and a Space key source; the tap target is a transparent full-canvas `rect`, so bots and people can always hit it.
